entry.title: MDF Is Strengthening America's Supply Chains

media:group.media:title: MDF Is Strengthening America's Supply Chains
media:group.media:description:
When critical materials become difficult to source, entire supply chains can be disrupted, affecting American manufacturing, energy production and national security. The Department of Energy’s Manufacturing Demonstration Facility (MDF) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory is helping strengthen domestic supply chains by connecting advanced manufacturing research with a vast network of U.S. industry partners. Through innovations such as big area additive manufacturing (BAAM), researchers are developing faster, more cost-effective production methods that reduce manufacturing complexity and help industry overcome supply chain challenges. Discover how MDF’s research capabilities, technology demonstrations and partnerships are helping American manufacturers build more resilient supply chains and reduce dependence on hard-to-source materials. Visit https://www.ornl.gov/mdf/. #ManufacturingInnovation
ORNL is using #BigScience to make a big impact. Learn more: https://www.ornl.gov/bigscience

entry.title: The Lux SI + HPC Supercomputer is Here

media:group.media:title: The Lux SI + HPC Supercomputer is Here
media:group.media:description:
A major new chapter in scientific computing begins at Oak Ridge National Laboratory: Lux is now open to scientific users.🎉
🤝 Made possible through a public-private partnership between the U.S. Department of Energy and AMD, Lux brings together super intelligence (SI) and high-performance computing to help researchers tackle complex, scientific challenges.
HPE helped bring Lux to life with its ProLiant Compute XD685 system. Powered by AMD GPUs, Lux pairs advanced SI capabilities with high-performance computing for modeling and simulation.
As one of the first systems supporting DOE’s Genesis Mission, Lux will enable research in areas including fusion energy, advanced materials and manufacturing, and Earth system prediction. About half of Lux’s annual computing time will support Genesis Mission projects, with the remainder available to AMD.
Lux expands the computing capacity available to American science and shows what sustained collaboration across government, research and industry can make possible.💫
🔗 More details on AmSC and the Genesis Mission: https://bit.ly/4BXWNXW

entry.title: ORNL demonstrates an agile drone manufacturing system at IMTS 2026

media:group.media:title: ORNL demonstrates an agile drone manufacturing system at IMTS 2026
media:group.media:description:
At the 2026 International Manufacturing Technology Show, ORNL showcased an agile drone manufacturing system that featured 3D printing of drone shells, automated robotic processing, and the latest development from its partnership with Mazak: a first-of-its-kind convergent platform that unifies metal additive manufacturing and high-precision machining within production-relevant workflows. Together, the system builds drones every 9 minutes and allows for molds to be adjusted as needed in real time.

entry.title: Large-scale 3D printing with ORNL-built mobile robots

media:group.media:title: Large-scale 3D printing with ORNL-built mobile robots
media:group.media:description: What if a 3D printer could move to create parts larger than its own reach? Researchers at DOE’s Manufacturing Demonstration Facility at ORNL developed a mobile additive manufacturing platform that can reposition itself and continue printing accurately. Using visual sensing, SI and advanced controls, the system expands the size of components that robots can produce beyond the limits of a fixed workspace.

entry.title: SMART AI: AI for next-generation fusion materials development

media:group.media:title: SMART AI: AI for next-generation fusion materials development
media:group.media:description:
Fusion power plants will demand structural materials that can withstand extreme temperatures, stress and irradiation over decades of service—and that can be manufactured reliably at industrial scale.
SMART-AI (Scale-Up and MAterial Reliability Translation AI), led by ORNL, is an AI/ML framework that unites experimental data, computational thermodynamics and structural descriptors to link processing, microstructure and performance. The platform will rapidly integrate diverse datasets, extrapolate to long-term service conditions and identify optimal material states under realistic industrial constraints. Beyond accelerating scale-up, SMART-AI could transform ASME code qualification—today a decades-long testing process—by providing validated predictive tools that speed up the deployment of advanced structural materials for fusion energy.
To learn more about this project, visit https://www.ornl.gov/projects/ai-next-generation-fusion-materials-development/

entry.title: SCINET: AI-powered operations for self-driving science research

media:group.media:title: SCINET: AI-powered operations for self-driving science research
media:group.media:description:
This project seeks to coordinate network traffic among agentic and scientific workflows across institutional boundaries. As DOE and other research organizations move toward AI-driven autonomous laboratories where robotics, edge AI, real-time analysis and intelligent feedback must operate seamlessly across distant locations, existing passive scientific networks have become bottlenecks that interfere with reliability and resilience. Distributed AI and agentic workflows need adaptive routing to prevent congestion, enable GPU-to-GPU transfers and take full advantage of 6G and accelerated network technology. SciNet, a science-aware platform for research network operations, will curate multimodal network operations data and tag packets with science project information to allow correlation of data from heterogeneous sources, handle sensitive data securely and anticipate network requirements to deliver shorter experimental latency, fewer workflow failures and faster discovery cycles across science domains to satisfy workflow needs.
To learn more about this project, visit https://www.ornl.gov/projects/ai-powered-operations-self-driving-science-research/

entry.title: AI-enabled discovery of rare earth elements

media:group.media:title: AI-enabled discovery of rare earth elements
media:group.media:description:
Heavy rare earth elements (REEs) are essential for modern industry, yet the United States relies heavily on imported supplies. Most of the world's heavy REEs come from deposits in Asia that formed as granite slowly broke down over time. In these deposits, the REEs are loosely attached to secondary minerals formed during weathering, making them easier to recover. Scientists still do not fully understand why these deposits become enriched with REEs, making it difficult to identify similar resources in the United States. This project will investigate how natural processes, including rock weathering, water infiltration, and landscape erosion, can move and concentrate REEs. The team will develop a physics-informed AI framework that integrates field observations, laboratory experiments, and computer models to improve predictions of where these deposits may occur. Initial work will focus on three granite watersheds in North Carolina. The resulting approach will speed the discovery of new domestic sources of heavy REEs across the southeastern United States.
To learn more about this project, visit https://www.ornl.gov/projects/ai-enabled-discovery-rare-earth-elements/

entry.title: PIPIT: AI-accelerated materials development and advanced manufacturing applications

media:group.media:title: PIPIT: AI-accelerated materials development and advanced manufacturing applications
media:group.media:description:
This project seeks to develop Pipit, an AI-based “foundation model factory” that will create custom foundation AI models that U.S. industry can leverage to accelerate materials development and the application of advanced manufacturing methods such as 3D printing. Foundation models hold the potential to revolutionize how insights and learned relationships are implemented across industrial enterprises, but realizing this potential requires extensive data generation and curation, AI model construction and training, and deployment on large-scale high-performance computing architectures. Pipit will provide an AI-enabled infrastructure that uses coding agents to convert prototype machine learning models into end-to-end foundation model pipelines. Pipit’s foundation models, benchmarks and data generated will be shared on the Genesis Mission platform for community use.
To learn more about this project, visit https://www.ornl.gov/projects/ai-accelerated-materials-development-and-advanced-manufacturing-applications/

media:group.media:title: FADO: Fusion Agentic Design Orchestrator
media:group.media:description:
The fusion pilot plant (FPP) vision cannot be realized without high-fidelity design simulations to reduce the risk associated with the first-of-a-kind device. A reliable digital representation of the design is needed to ensure an understanding of the facility’s performance, to optimize control systems, and to identify no-go designs. However, code complexity necessitates a team of experts to perform the analysis, posing a substantial barrier to entry for new users without access to these powerful but highly complex simulation frameworks. Additionally, high-fidelity modeling and simulation often focus on the device design without considering maintenance, robotics, or construction. These considerations should be at the forefront of fusion design because Reliability, Availability, Maintainability, and Inspectability, known as the RAMI principles, directly impact economic viability. This proposal will address these gaps by developing an agentic workflow to demonstrate the AI advantage in automating the time-consuming and difficult process of setting up and executing high-fidelity simulations for fusion systems. The Fusion Agentic Design Orchestrator will support fusion design by integrating high-performance computing modeling tools, RAMI principles, and robotics considerations, within a unified virtual environment.
To learn more about this project, visit https://www.ornl.gov/projects/ai-assisted-fusion-power-plant-designs/.

entry.title: NEUROMORPHIC: Low-energy AI for scientific discovery

media:group.media:title: NEUROMORPHIC: Low-energy AI for scientific discovery
media:group.media:description:
This project seeks to leverage neuromorphic computing and spiking neural networks to analyze scientific data at unprecedented rates and scales with lower costs and higher speeds than conventional AI while maintaining equivalent accuracy. Current AI models carry high operational costs, are computationally expensive and consume vast amounts of power. Neuromorphic processors, which mimic the operation of neurons in the human brain, consume from a thousand to ten thousand times less energy than existing CPUs or GPUs yet remain capable of performing the same parallel computations. This neuromorphic advantage, when used effectively, holds the potential to achieve AI-driven autonomous laboratories that dramatically advance U.S. scientific leadership and economic competitiveness at greatly reduced expense. These spiking neural networks will be integrated with the Genesis Mission and run on the American Science Cloud, with results shared for community use.
To learn more about this project, visit https://www.ornl.gov/projects/low-energy-ai-scientific-discovery/.
